correctness.rationale: Every labeled strict complete preference profile for n=2 and n=3 is examined, as are all n! perfect matchings and all off-matching blocking pairs. This exhaustive exact-integer proof determines full Nash and regret optimizer sets and verifies all n=2,3 outcomes, including 3,504 different-regret matching comparisons. The n=4 witness is exactly checked against all 24 matchings, producing three stable matchings with unique opposing optima. The analytical embedding forces each new mutual-top pair into all stable matchings, shifts original ranks uniformly and preserves Nash product comparisons up to a positive common factor for every n>=4. All quantifiers and normalization assumptions agree between claim and proof. This is not a random sample or an infinite computational assertion.

originality.rationale: The relevant 2026 primary full text develops the Nash-welfare algorithm and fairness experiments but not this sharp small-market Nash/minimum-regret set inclusion and labeled census. value.rationale: The sharp threshold answers a natural substantive fairness question: whether maximizing geometric-mean rank utility automatically minimizes the worst individual partner rank. At n<=3 this is a full guarantee with exact frequencies of optimizer-set agreement; an explicit incompatible n=4 profile and exact all-larger-market embedding show precisely where it stops. The result informs choosing a fairness objective in small stable matching markets and is not merely a renamed count, arbitrary parameter slice or recitation of the general Nash algorithm. The exact limitation is strict, complete, balanced markets with utility n-r; it does not claim broad social-welfare approximation.
